summary: Iteration 2 retest of Neon RPS dApp focused on the NEW features: Coinbase Onramp session endpoint, BUY BASE ETH UI on Home/Create/Footer, and the 404 GAME NOT FOUND fallback on /game/:id. Backend: 7/7 pytest checks PASS, including the new POST /api/onramp/session happy path (real Coinbase Developer Platform call returned a session token; URL starts with https://pay.coinbase.com/buy/select-asset?sessionToken= and contains defaultNetwork=base & defaultAsset=ETH). Both validation cases (missing wallet, bad eth address) return 422 as expected. Existing endpoints /api/healthz, /api/health (node_api=true), /api/og/game/1 (PNG), /api/share/g/1 (OG meta + refresh) still pass. Frontend: Home shows BUY BASE ETH button, /create shows WALLET REQUIRED panel + BUY BASE ETH, /game/1 now correctly renders the 404 GAME NOT FOUND state with [data-testid=game-not-found], RETURN TO LOBBY and START NEW DUEL buttons (the perpetual-loader bug from iteration 1 is fixed). /leaderboard and /treasury load. Footer also contains a buy-base-eth-btn (count=2 on home). Clicking BUY BASE ETH with no wallet does NOT crash the app.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/onramp.py cleanly handles 32-byte and 64-byte Ed25519 key encodings, uses 120s JWT expiry, fresh nonce per request — correct CDP JWT auth implementation.
FastAPI /api/onramp/session is registered BEFORE the catch-all /api/{path:path} proxy, so it is served by FastAPI directly and not forwarded to Node — correct ordering.
OnrampSessionRequest validates wallet_address with regex ^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$ via Pydantic — Field-level validation correctly yields 422 on bad/missing input.
Coinbase API errors are surfaced with status 502 and bounded detail (<=500 chars) which is good for debugging without leaking full payloads.
Onramp response model only exposes {url, expires_in} — session token only lives inside the URL parameters which is acceptable for a hosted-purchase flow (token is short-lived 5 min).

Frontend BuyBaseEthButton click without a wallet connected does not open the WalletConnect modal in our test — the button likely no-ops silently when no address is available. Consider explicitly calling openConnectModal() when isConnected=false so users understand why nothing happens. Not a crash, but UX could be clearer.
Console still shows several HTTP 413 (Payload Too Large) errors from external WalletConnect/relay endpoints — same as iteration 1, doesn't affect functionality.
